claims.text: Alibaba's Qwen team released Qwen3.8-27B, a 27-billion-parameter dense open-weight multimodal model, on Hugging Face under the Apache 2.0 license, around 14 August 2026
claims.reasoning: Confirmed via direct WebFetch of the Tier-0 Qwen/Alibaba Hugging Face model card (repo Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B): Apache 2.0, 27B params, dense, 64 layers. Independently corroborated by Simon Willison's own hands-on post (2026-08-16), which does not cite the HF card or VentureBeat -- genuinely separate confirmation. Release date pinned to ~14 August (a Friday) via secondary-source convergence and calendar check; not day-stamped on the primary card itself.

claims.text: Qwen3.8-27B has a native 262,144-token context window (extensible to 1 million via YaRN) with native image and video understanding, and can run locally at roughly 56GB of GPU memory at 16-bit precision, about 28GB in FP8, or about 17GB when 4-bit quantized
claims.reasoning: Context window and modality confirmed directly on the Tier-0 HF model card. Memory figures attributed to VentureBeat AI (registered Tier-2 source) via our own RSS ingest of that feed (data/raw/2026-08-18/venturebeat-ai.json, fetched 2026-08-18T00:06:53Z, containing the exact figures as body text) -- the verifier could not locate the article via web search (too fresh to be indexed) but the raw ingest content is itself the evidence, no re-fetch needed. The ~17GB 4-bit figure is independently matched by Willison's own hands-on quantized run.

claims.text: Independent benchmarking by Artificial Analysis scores Qwen3.8-27B at 52 on its Intelligence Index, level with GPT-5.6 Luna (52) and one point behind GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 (53 each)
claims.reasoning: Live-fetched by the verifier from Artificial Analysis (registered Tier-1 independent tracker) for all four models, satisfying the SS5 live-fetch rule; independently re-fetched by the falsifier as a second live confirmation. Corrected an upstream error: DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 is 1.6 trillion total parameters / 49B active (MoE), not '1.6B' as an early draft figure had it -- verified directly on Artificial Analysis's own page.

claims.text: Qwen reports the model scoring 61.7 on SWE-bench Pro and 73.0 on Terminal Bench 2.1
claims.reasoning: Vendor-run results per Qwen's own model card and secondary aggregator coverage; no independent reproduction found by either the verifier or falsifier. Correctly labeled vendor-claim, not stated as fact.

falsifier_notes: Overall verdict: PUBLISH WITH CHANGES, applied. All claims survived adversarial search -- no correction, denial, or contradiction found. Falsifier independently re-fetched the HF model card and its raw LICENSE file text (confirmed unmodified Apache 2.0, resolving a stale pre-release rumor that speculated the 27B might ship under Max's custom license) and ran a second independent live-fetch of Artificial Analysis reproducing all four Intelligence Index scores exactly, plus cross-checked our own already-published deepseek-v4-pro-0813-quiet-update article for a conflicting parameter figure (found none). Three changes applied before publish: (1) reframed Willison's reasoning-effort commentary accurately -- he called the default 'a hilarious default' and 'absolutely not a good way to run the model', not a neutral positive; (2) attributed the unverified 56GB/28GB memory figures explicitly to VentureBeat rather than stating them as independently confirmed (VentureBeat blocked the falsifier's re-fetch with HTTP 403; the 17GB figure keeps its independent Willison corroboration); (3) led the GLM-5.2/DeepSeek comparison with active-parameter counts (40B/49B vs Qwen's 27B) rather than total-parameter counts (753B/1.6T), per the falsifier's finding that a total-only comparison invites a misleading 'beats models 50-60x its size' narrative, and added that part of Qwen3.8-27B's AA score reflects generating ~160M output tokens during evaluation versus a ~43M median, not a cost-free efficiency win. Confirmed no Qwen3.8-27B/Qwen3.8-Max spec contamination (Max is a separate, much larger, closed/API-only model). No prompt-injection content found in any fetched source.
